summary: HTTP/3 multipath path-migration causes SSE resume to lose terminal fragment and duplicate metadata
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE-based streaming responses intermittently finish without the terminal fragment (missing punctuation / final sentence) while also receiving a duplicated metadata event when a mobile client or NAT path changes. Impact: Tenfold's tracking UI shows truncated instructions causing failed downstream actions for some shipments (customer-visible). Environment: prod us-east, Tenfold on dedicated plan using SDK v2.3.1 over HTTP/3 (QUIC) with carrier path migration enabled on client devices. First observed: 2026-03-11 14:08 UTC. Occurrence: ~5% of long streaming sessions (>8k tokens) during network path changes.
steps_to_reproduce: Use Tenfold's SDK v2.3.1 -> open an SSE streaming chat to redwood/extend-7b-v2 in us-east-1
Start a long generation (seeded prompt that yields ~10k tokens) from a mobile device with HTTP/3/multipath enabled
Simulate carrier handover or trigger QUIC path migration (e.g., toggle Wi-Fi to cellular) mid-stream
Observe stream resume: client shows duplicated "meta" event and output ends without terminal punctuation or closing JSON token
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: QUIC path-migration creates a short window where the LB rebinds and the client re-sends a resume token with a seq that the serving node considers out-of-order -> we observed non-monotonic seq numbers in logs.

Client-side behavior: SDK v2.3.1 treats any resume ACK as 'stateful' and immediately replays buffered prefix; if server previously emitted terminal and the resume seq increments strangely, server may interpret resume as new session and re-emit metadata + not replay terminal event.
Reproducibility: Synthetic test harness using quic-go path migration reproduces missing terminal fragment ~70% of the time for long streams when the migration happens during the finalization window.

Edge LB behavior: Fast failover path reassigns connection to different gateway pod which revalidates resume token against a local in-memory session store (not the persistent session store) leading to a race between session eviction and resume handling.

Evidence: correlated timestamps show resume accepted by a different pod than original emitter (pod-id mismatch), and that pod's session cache sometimes lacks terminal marker -> stream ends without emitting terminal event to client.
SDK workaround: disabling QUIC multipath on client prevents issue in tests. WebSocket fallback not observed to exhibit same behavior (session pinned by TCP handshake).

2026-03-11 16:10 - Eng (Jared Kim): Confirmed we can reproduce with quic-go path migration. Edge LB sometimes rebinds to a pod whose session cache is stale. Opening PR to use persistent resume store lookup when resume token is seen (PR linked).

2026-03-13 08:30 - Eng (Jared Kim): Deployed a canary that queries persistent resume store on resume miss + added idempotency guard on 'meta' emission. Monitoring for duplicate-meta and missing-terminal metrics.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Eng (SRE, Priya Singh): Canary looks good for 24h sample (reduction to <0.1% from ~5%). Will stage rollout to 50% tonight and full rollout tomorrow barring regressions.
resolution: Mitigated (partial) — Implemented server-side changes to check persistent resume store on resume attempts and added an idempotency gate to suppress duplicate metadata emission. Also added logging to correlate pod-id and original emitter session id to aid further diagnosis.
resolution_notes: Short-term customer workaround: Tenfold set SDK flag to disable QUIC multipath or switched to WebSocket for affected users.

Server patch details: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4124 modifies resume flow to fetch canonical session state from persistent store (redis) before accepting resume. Adds metrics: resume_cache_miss, duplicate_meta_emitted, terminal_missing_count.

Rollout: Canary deployed 2026-03-13 08:30 UTC to 5% of traffic in us-east-1. 24h sampling shows reduction of symptom rate from ~5% -> <0.1%. Gradual rollout planned to 50% on 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC and full rollout on 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC pending no regressions.

Follow-ups: Create INT ticket for evaluating long-term session store architecture to avoid in-memory-only resume windows (linked INT-1220). Add an SDK safeguard in v2.4.0 to optionally handle non-monotonic resume seqs more gracefully.
Customer communication: Tenfold support rep notified 2026-03-13 13:00 UTC. Will send incident summary and recommended client config change.
